title: Telescopes fire lasers into the sky to make fake stars 90 km up

cover.alt: Four thin orange laser beams rise straight up into a starry night sky from between two telescope enclosures.
cover.credit: ESO/F. Kamphues/S. Lowery/G. Hüdepohl · CC BY 4.0

body: Turbulence in the air blurs the light of stars before it reaches a telescope. **Adaptive optics** can undo the blur, but it needs a bright reference star to measure it against, and stars that bright are not found in every part of the sky. So big observatories make their own: a laser tuned to 589.2 nanometres excites sodium atoms in a thin layer about 90 km up, and the glowing spot acts as an artificial star wherever the telescope points.

slides.alt: Four parallel orange laser beams in a starry sky; the camera tilts down to the telescope enclosure they rise from, then a time-lapse shows the beams slanting up over several telescope buildings as clouds drift past.
slides.caption: April 2016, Paranal, Chile: four lasers on the Very Large Telescope fire into the sky at their first light. The camera follows the beams down, then a time-lapse shows the site.
slides.credit: ESO/F. Kamphues/S. Lowery/G. Hüdepohl · CC BY 4.0 · excerpt

slides.heading: How a fake star sharpens the view

steps.label: A laser makes sodium atoms 90 km up glow
The telescope measures the spot’s blur

slides.prompt: How powerful is each of the four lasers on the Very Large Telescope?
slides.detail: Each beam leaves the telescope 30 cm wide. Together they make four artificial stars over Paranal.

slides.label: the wavelength of the laser: the yellow-orange of sodium
slides.text: Sodium atoms in the mesosphere absorb light of exactly this colour and give it off again, so the spot where the beam hits the layer shines.

slides.question: Why don’t astronomers just use a real star as their reference?
options: Real stars are too far away
slides.explanation: Stars bright enough for adaptive optics are not common enough to appear in all parts of the sky, so a laser star lets it work wherever the telescope points.
